deals.notes: Regency Court at Woodfield is a 139,913 SF, Publix- and Walgreens-anchored community center built in 1992 on ±14.85 acres at the signalized corner of Yamato Rd & Jog Rd (±77,500 VPD) at the entrance to Woodfield Country Club in central Boca Raton (Boca Raton West submarket). The trade area is exceptionally affluent — 1-mile average HH income of $264,527 and average home value of $1,118,348 (90% / 73% above Palm Beach County). Publix (#0428, 42,112 SF) is a standout at $46.1M / $1,095 PSF in 2025 (13% above Publix's chain average) on a low $7.50 PSF base + 1% percentage rent over a $31.58M breakpoint, with a ~1.9% health ratio. Both anchors are original 1992 tenants paying well below market and roll within ~6 years — but on CURRENT contractual terms the rent roll shows Walgreens expiring 11/30/2026 (option to 11/30/2031) and Publix 12/9/2027 (option to 12/2032), producing a short current-term WALT of ~2.7 years. The value-add thesis: mark-to-market of 81,543 SF (67% of occupied GLA, >$1.0M upside), lease-up of 13,927 SF of vacancy (10% of GLA), and anchor renewal/expansion (Publix has discussed a 47,240 SF expansion) or re-tenanting. The OM's In-Place Pro-Forma rent roll ties exactly to In-Place NOI of $3,651,460 (EGI $5,552,746 − OpEx $1,901,286); the T-12 actual NOI (Apr-25–Mar-26) was $2,965,093 on $5.16M income and $2.20M opex. Shops are high-performing and seasoned (avg shop sales $651 PSF, 9.1% health ratio, 14.5-yr tenure). Debt-free and offered unpriced by CBRE National Retail Partners; key risks are concentrated near-term anchor rollover (incl. a Walgreens 2026 break), Walgreens' BB- credit and soft reported sales, and a Chase co-tenancy tied to Publix occupancy.
keyAssumptions: RENT ROLL FULLY EXTRACTED: base rents, lease start/end, expense recoveries, percentage rent and sales for all tenants are from the OM's In-Place Pro-Forma rent roll (the separate text-readable rent-roll PDF Eric provided). The In-Place Pro-Forma ties out: occupied minimum rent $3,694,627 + recoveries $1,538,499 + percentage rent $319,620 = EGI $5,552,746; less OpEx $1,901,286 = NOI $3,651,460 (the OM headline).

ANCHOR TERMS VERIFIED AGAINST EXECUTED LEASES: Publix automatic-extension letter (4/6/2022) confirms term to 12/9/2027 with 1 remaining 5-year option (→12/9/2032); Walgreens recorded Memorandum (1992) confirms 12,422 SF. The rent roll shows Walgreens' CURRENT term ending 11/30/2026 with a 5-year option/continuation to 11/30/2031 — i.e. a potential near-term (2026) break/option, sooner than the OM's '2031' headline. Confirm the 2026 date in the executed Walgreens lease.

In-Place NOI $3,651,460 is the OM's normalized pro-forma (current leases, vacancy at $0); T-12 actual NOI was $2,965,093. Recovery type is NNN for essentially all tenants (Pro-Rata + Mgmt + a 15% admin fee on CAM for most shops; several carry a 5% cumulative CAM cap).
Tax bill (assessed $42,205,863; ad valorem $688,917 + non-ad-valorem $124,038 = $812,955) is per the 2025 Palm Beach County bill, net of a 4% early-payment discount.

Some shop leases commence later in 2026 (new/renewal leases): Pepe's (10/2026), Crema (5/2026), 16 Handles (5/2026), Boca Best (7/2026), Move with Studios (7/2026), Avant Gallery (temp, 4/2026). Avant Gallery (B015) is a temporary tenant paying 10% of gross sales (no base rent; ~$150k projected) and is assumed to vacate after stabilizing Year 1.

redFlags.description: Very short current-term WALT (~2.7 years) from concentrated near-term anchor rollover: on CURRENT contractual terms Walgreens (12,422 SF) expires 11/30/2026 and Publix (42,112 SF, 30% of GLA) 12/9/2027. Both have one 5-year option (to 2031 / 2032) but are well below market — the thesis depends on renewing/re-tenanting both. Execution, downtime, and the 2026 Walgreens decision are the central risks.

10% vacancy (13,927 SF across A014, B020-22, C006, C007) — the In-Place Pro-Forma carries it at $0; lease-up cost/time risk. Several other suites have current leases expiring 2026–2028 (FrameWorld 12/2026, Boca Beauty Nail 12/2026, Apolonia 10/2027, Better Me 12/2027, Chase 5/2027), adding rollover.

Walgreens credit is BB- (S&P) and its REPORTED sales are soft/declining ($197.84 PSF reported 2025; the OM adjusts to ~$822 PSF by adding back 3rd-party-plan Rx sales excluded from reported figures — the reported figure is the contractual percentage-rent basis).

Chase Bank (B022-24) co-tenancy/go-dark: Chase may cease operating if Publix is vacant 90+ days, with base rent abating until ≥75% of the Publix premises is re-occupied by a single retailer; after one year of reduced rent Chase must terminate or resume — anchor-dependent income during any Publix transition.

Anchor income is deeply below market and partly percentage-rent dependent (Publix base $7.50 PSF + 1% over a $31.58M breakpoint); in-place yield is low relative to a trophy price — returns rely on realizing the mark-to-market.

Environmental: property enrolled in Florida's Dry Cleaning Solvent program (former dry cleaner, Suite B012 / now The UPS Store). Aug-2025 report met No Further Action criteria and FDEP confirmed closure 12/15/2025, but the formal Site Rehabilitation Completion Order (SRCO) and site restoration were still pending as of the OM.

upsideItems.detail: 81,543 SF (67% of occupied GLA), incl. Publix ($7.50) and Walgreens ($14.50), is ~36% below market (current avg $22.88 vs market $35.59 PSF) — >$1.0M of identified rent upside over a 10-year hold.
13,927 SF (10% of GLA) of available space (incl. the 6,191 SF B020-22 block) in an infill, 98.4%-occupied submarket with shop asking rents of $45–$55 PSF NNN.

Publix is below market at $7.50 PSF and has expressed interest in waiving its remaining option and renewing early, and in an expanded 47,240 SF prototype store — new South FL grocer rents are mid-to-upper $20s PSF.
With Walgreens' near-term (2026) break, renew at market, re-tenant the 12,422 SF box, or convert/divide it into higher-rent shop space; Walgreens has relocation rights.
In-place shop leases carry ~3% annual / stepped increases (and 15% CAM admin recovery), contributing to the projected 94% / 6.8% CAGR 10-year NOI growth.
